    "severity": "medium",
    "file": "t14.js",
    "line": 4,
    "evidence": "document.getElementById(\"results-title\").innerHTML = \"Results for \" + term;",
    "llm_reasoning": "While primarily a security risk, using .innerHTML for simple text injection is a performance anti-pattern. The browser must invoke the HTML parser to process the string, which is significantly slower than using .textContent. In high-frequency updates or large DOM trees, this triggers unnecessary layout recalculations and potential re-parsing of the DOM subtree.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use .textContent instead: document.getElementById(\"results-title\").textContent = \"Results for \" + term;",
    "confidence": 0.9,

      "performance"
    ]
  }
